MIT.summary: A short, permissive license: use, copy, change and share it for any purpose, including commercial work, as long as the copyright and license notices stay attached.

Apache-2.0.summary: Permissive like MIT, with an express patent grant from contributors and a requirement to state the changes you made.

BSD-3-Clause.summary: Permissive like MIT, plus a clause barring use of the copyright holder's or contributors' names to promote derived products without consent.

GPL-3.0.summary: Strong copyleft: free to use, study and change, but distributed copies and derivative works must stay under this license with source code available.

GPL-2.0.summary: The older strong-copyleft GPL: distributed copies and derivative works must stay under this license with source code available.

AGPL-3.0.summary: Strong copyleft like GPL-3.0, extended to network use: offering a modified version as a service means offering its source code too.

MPL-2.0.summary: Weak, file-level copyleft: changes to the licensed files must be shared under the MPL, but a larger work combining them can stay under different terms.

BSD-3-Clause / AGPL-3.0.summary: Mixed licensing: most of the repository is permissive BSD-3-Clause, while the server components (management, signal, relay, combined) are copyleft AGPL-3.0.

BSD-2-Clause.summary: Permissive like MIT: use, copy, change and share for any purpose, as long as the copyright notice and license text stay with redistributed source or binaries.

GPL-3.0-or-later.summary: Strong copyleft: free to use, study and change, but distributed copies and derivative works must stay under this license with source available. You may choose version 3 or any later version.

AGPL-3.0-or-later.summary: Strong copyleft like GPL-3.0, extended to network use: offering a modified version as a service means offering its source to the users. You may choose version 3 or any later version.

GPL-2.0 / GPL-3.0.summary: Dual choice: the project is offered under GPL version 2 or, at your option, version 3. Both are strong copyleft licenses that require source to stay available in distributed copies and derivative works.

AGPL-3.0 / GPL-3.0.summary: Mixed licensing across repositories: the app is AGPL-3.0 and the server is GPL-3.0. Both are strong copyleft; AGPL also covers offering a modified version as a network service. Check each repository.

GPL-2.0-or-later.summary: Strong copyleft: free to use, study and change, but distributed copies and derivative works must stay under this license with source available. You may choose version 2 or any later version.

LGPL-3.0.summary: Weak copyleft: you may use the software and link it from other programs, but changes to the library itself must be shared under the same license.

PostgreSQL.summary: Permissive license for PostgreSQL: use, copy, change and distribute with the copyright and permission notices retained. Extensions may use other licenses.

EUPL-1.2.summary: A copyleft license covering the current Pi-hole core, DNS engine and web interface. Source and license obligations apply when distributing or communicating covered work; older code and bundled dependencies can have separate terms.
